Manaus grew during the rubber boom of the 19th century. One of the most striking landmarks of that era is the Amazonas Theater, with its neoclassical architecture and colorful dome.

From Manaus, travelers can venture into the jungle for several days. The program includes a lodge, boat trips, fishing, a night safari, visits to local settlements and opportunities to observe pink river dolphins.

Another memorable experience is the Meeting of the Waters of the Rio Negro and the Amazon River. Their differently colored currents flow side by side for some distance before mixing.

## Surfing, Waves and Nightlife: What to See in Máncora, Peru

### Máncora — A Destination for Surfers!

The village of Máncora lies on a Pacific Ocean bay near the border with Ecuador. Some of the highest and longest waves on the planet can be found here.

## Holidays in Máncora

### Máncora — A Tourist Center!

The area is best known as an affordable vacation destination and a place for some of the most extreme surfing. Long ago, Máncora was just a small fishing village. Today, however, it has grown into a modern tourist center with fairly well-developed infrastructure, lively nightlife and unspoiled nature. Máncora has one of the cleanest beaches in the world, and local people are exceptionally welcoming. In addition, the surrounding area offers opportunities to admire wildlife and Inca archaeological sites.

Manta, also known as San Pablo de Manta, is in Manabí Province. The city existed in pre-Columbian times and remains one of the country's major maritime centers today: Manta is considered Ecuador's second-largest port.

Tuna fishing plays an important role in Manta's economy. The resort area also caters to young travelers, with plenty of inexpensive summer tourist camps, nightclubs, bars and restaurants.

One episode of the 18th-century French expedition to measure the position of the equator is connected with Manta. Charles Marie de La Condamine arrived at its port in 1735.

## Beaches, Jungle and Sloths: What to See in Manuel Antonio, Costa Rica

Manuel Antonio is a popular resort with beaches and coastal jungle. It has bustling shopping centers geared toward tourists, open-air bars and seafood restaurants.

## Manuel Antonio National Park

Manuel Antonio National Park is a natural gem of Costa Rica, situated near the country's oldest resort on the Pacific coast. This small reserve covers just 683 hectares. It was established in 1972 to protect the exceptionally beautiful landscapes and rich flora and fauna of the Pacific coast.

Manuel Antonio is a small town on the Pacific coast. It is home to the national park and magnificent white-sand beaches. The rich underwater world, with unusual plants and fish, attracts diving enthusiasts. You can also take a walk through the town's picturesque surroundings.
